To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Protein synthesis inhibitors prevent consolidation of LTP only in depleted slices, but not in non-depleted slices, 2) Protein synthesis inhibitors do not prevent consolidation of LPT when LTP is induced in a non-depleted slice and then the slice is depleted, and 3) LTP induction in a slice induces a protein synthesis-dependent process that stabilizes LTP in depleted slices.
the protein synthesis inhibitors did not affect LTP when applied after TBS, and that the inhibitors prevented LTP in slices depleted of protein by prior incubation.
the protein synthesis required for consolidation of LTP is not necessary for its induction, but is necessary to prepare neurons to respond to subsequent induction of LTP.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cellular and molecular processes that support the consolidation of memory
the molecular and cellular processes underlying the consolidation of memory.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the consolidation of memory-related plasticity in the mammalian brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the consolidation of long-term memory requires the production of new proteins, and that the synthesis of new proteins is a necessary condition for the consolidation of memory.
the consolidation process is a multi-step process that includes the formation of new proteins that are required for subsequent learning.
memory formation and consolidation are not dependent on protein synthesis but rather are dependent on a series of complex signaling processes that stabilize synaptic changes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

protein synthesis is not required for consolidation of memory-related changes in synaptic strength, but is required for consolidation of changes in the synaptic cytoskeleton that are necessary to support those changes in synaptic strength.
protein synthesis is required to support memory consolidation but not for the consolidation of synaptic changes per se.
the actin cytoskeletal changes that support LTP, and likely memory, are established in two phases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the consolidation of memory is not simply a matter of new proteins being synthesized and incorporated into synapses. Rather
protein synthesis is not required for LTP consolidation.
memory formation is not simply a matter of protein synthesis.
